Through the extended metaphor of a failing university building and its endless, noisy repairs, the story offers unique and thought-provoking insights into human nature and institutional life. Specifically, it explores what the narrator calls the "quiet scandal" of human adaptability—not the suffering itself, "but the speed with which suffering becomes décor." It also provides a poignant perspective on how shared endurance of mundane, bureaucratic dysfunction can create a "grim membership" and a strange sense of attachment, to the point where a person might actually miss the chaos and discomfort once the problem is finally resolved.
